title: Open Composer: A Web-Based Application for Generating and Managing Batch Jobs on HPC Clusters
problem: Submitting batch jobs on HPC clusters requires familiarity with Linux commands and job schedulers, creating a significant learning barrier for beginners and reducing HPC accessibility
motivation: HPC resources remain underutilized due to steep learning curves for job submission and management. A user-friendly interface can democratize HPC access and reduce training burden on support staff.
method: A web application built on the Open OnDemand platform that makes it easy to submit jobs (computational tasks) to supercomputers without learning Linux commands. When users access the application, they fill out a form specifying their needs—like how many computers to use and how long the job should run—and the application generates the shell script (the command sequence) required for submission. Users can view the generated script, edit it directly for more control, submit the job, track its progress, and save parameters from previous jobs to reuse later.
key_novelty: The key innovation is providing both automatic script generation and manual editing in one tool, so beginners can get started easily while advanced users can customize fully.
contributions: Web-based batch job composition interface reducing Linux/scheduler learning requirements
Automatic shell script generation from web forms with real-time preview
Direct script editing capability maintaining flexibility for advanced users
Unified interface for job submission and status monitoring
Support for reusable job parameters and dynamic form widgets
Preprocessing steps support for job preparation
Portability across various HPC clusters via Open OnDemand integration
hardware_target: Any system running Open OnDemand framework

metrics.secondary: Error rate reduction in job scripts

limitations: Abstract-only analysis; no quantitative evaluation data provided; usability study not detailed; comparison with other HPC portal solutions not mentioned
